description: Glitch Armor is a protective spell inspired by the nuanced experience of visibility within queer communities. On one hand, being visible allows them to be their full authentic selves, occupy space, exist, and find others alike. On the other hand, being visible exposes them to emotional and physical violence. This 3D animated couple reacts to movement in the room through a live camera feed. In turn, the glitch effect takes place and renders them progressively less visible.
What if technology had evolved to have human personality traits?
What if digital characters also had anxiety about being visibly queer?

Glitch Armor represents an exercise in character design, utilizing interactive technology as another layer for storytelling. As more viewers get closer to the installation, the characters display their personalities, anxiety, and rebellious thoughts.

projects.title: Look Again

gallery.caption: Prototype 02, Python script, Looking at a physical object

description: This project explores “low-tech” Computer Vision through a simple script written in Python. Using the NumPy library and a webcam, it enables the computer to interpret visual data in a more human-like way. Instead of processing thousands of individual pixels and RGB values, the script simplifies the image data, resulting in larger pixel areas and their median color. These are then compared with a small database to identify the closest color.

gallery.caption: Imported body part as an .fbx file in TD
Opportunity for optimization, all these nodes could be a simpler script

description: More information in the associated log.
This project was created in the context of a course. Due to lack of time, I wasn't able to finish it satisfactorily. I plan to update it in the coming months.

To Dissect / To Stitch is a digital puzzle made of my own 3D scanned body, inspired by academic literature in queer theory. The final piece acts as a manifesto regarding body-related and perception-based societal norms. In the end, I see it as a kind of auto-ethnographic process where I was able to analyze the external perception, as well as my own, of my body, both in a deconstructed and reconstructed state. With MediaPipe, a machine learning tool, the viewer in front of a visual composition of myself with heavy medical and 'objective' undertones can replace the pieces back in place using hand gestures. The experience is complete when the viewer sees the whole manifesto written in the place of a previously dry descriptions of each body parts.

projects.title: Post-Apocalyptic Hottie

gallery.caption: Displacement map used for the ground block

description: This character tells a futuristic story, where fashion is still a priority even after the environment became hostile. I imagine people in this alternate universe having to cover up entirely to protect themselves from the polluted air and intense UV rays.

In this character design exercise, the personal protective equipment takes the shape of a pair of plateform boots, a helmet with anti-UV glasses, a skin-tight shirt to show off defined chest muscles, puffy leather pants and gloves. To complete the outfit, a cute shoulder bag that matches the boots and helmet along with a phone capting atmospheric information are added as accessories.
This high-ploygon count sculpted character is brought to life using Mixamo, a motion capture library. The textures are painted and generated with Substance Designer and Substance Painter.

projects.title: Awakening of the Frog

gallery.caption: Focus on the frog, still from the turntable animation
Focus on the pond, still from the turntable animation

description: In the form of a low-poly animated diorama, Awakening of the Frog tells the story of an adored demon toad, set in a whimsical and mysterious environment. In this creative exploration of a satanical and natural theme, the scene comes alive with carefully designed plants and animals that interact subtly, revealing a rich narrative through their positionning and behavior. The centerpiece, a winged toad with scary teeth, floats in the air while all the attention of the other smaller creatures that inhabit this surreal world is directed on it.

The diorama features a softly animated backdrop, generated with Substance Designer, to enhance the dreamlike atmosphere. The rest of the environment, including the detailed models, the stylized textures, and the moody lighting, is entirely crafted in Blender 3D. Minimal yet purposeful animations such as blood dripping from the frog breathe life into the scene, inviting viewers to immerse themselves in its story.

projects.title: Les Daltons s'évadent!
description: Les Daltons s'évadent! (The Daltons Escape!) is a 2D game inspired by the action-packed adventures of Lucky Luke, a vintage cartoon about a lone cowboy chasing down the Dalton brothers. These four criminals are always planning their next coup, and are infamous outlaws in the american west. Most often, their ambitious bank robberies put them in trouble, as they always end up back in the state prison, only to plot yet another escape attempt.
I grew up loving this TV show and couldn’t resist the chance to relive those childhood memories by creating this short narrative prison break game.

This game was created in the conext of a programming class. Because this is a very simple one, both visually and conceptually, I was able to spend time of animations and composition. This minimalist style is out of my comfort zone, but i find the product very bold and fun.

description: bodymod is an experimental sandbox 2D game, with a few elements of generative art. It's also a reflection about body modification and body agency. Growing up gay, I've been subjected to a lot of microaggressions and rarely felt pretty and confident. I have often fantasized about being able to completly change the way I look, either to scare others or to be accepted by them.

Taking agency over how my body looks like made me realize two things. First, I want to look different and I can be different. Second, it's possible to achieve that and have confidence in who I am and how I present myself without the valiation of others. Getting tattoos and piercings, dying my hair, and dressing the way I want felt liberating and powerful at first, and it still feels the same now. This idea of body modification as a way to feel in control of my mental state is the overall message I wanted to convey.

Overall, I wanted the mood of this game to be dark, mysterious, and unpredictable. I think modifying your body in real life induce similar feelings, as you never fully know what will happen and how you will react. It's exciting and mildly scary… Are you ready to leap into it?

projects.title: EFFA - Visual Identity

gallery.caption: A few word on the choices of typography, color, and style

description: This visual identity was developped in the context of a graphic design class during my - unfinished - bachelor degree in Industrial Design at Universié de Montréal. We were all prompted to create posters, book covers, and other merchandise for the next iteration of EFFA (Exposition des finissants de la Faculté de l'aménagement).

The theme being 'CTRL+S', I went with a design sporting heavy contrast, fine lines, and repeating typography. My inspiration for these choices came from an exploration of the theme that could be resumed in three words: Nervosité, Écho, and Arts Numériques (translation: Nervousness, Echos, and Digital Arts).

projects.title: Pyre
description: Pyre is a small, portable barbecue concept developed during my (unfinished) degree in Industrial Design at Université de Montréal. This project was created for the Hudson's Bay Company (HBC), with a strong emphasis on branding. It needed to be marketed to their mid-to-high-end customer base, be portable, and above all, safe to use.

After researching metal sheet bending and assembly, I came up with this sleek and original stackable design. For instance, with just six tabs on the lid and six corresponding notches in the base, the lid securely stays in place. This approach not only provides an elegant form but also ensures that the object's fabrication and assembly are straightforward and cost-effective.

interests.title: 3D Animation
interests.summary: Creating a digital product with 3D software.
interests.description: When I say I do 3D animation, I mean mostly everything that can happen in a 3D software. That's modelling, remeshing, UV mapping, texturing, rigging, animating, lighting, simulating physics, and compositing. Not every project requires all steps, but I am familiar with and deeply enjoy this overall process.

interests.title: Tattooing
interests.summary: Marking the skin permanently with needles and ink.
interests.description: I have always been drawn to the tattoing process, both to decorate my own body and others. I find body modification enticing because it takes effort and pain, making it something significant and giving it grounding properties.

interests.title: Creative Coding
interests.summary: Programming as a tool for creative expression.
interests.description: I started learning to code a few years ago, and I now am pretty decent at HTML/CSS, Javascript, and Python. These languages opened up so many doors for me, and most of my current projects include some kind of script.

interests.title: Interactive Technologies
interests.summary: Systems, devices, or software designed to enable real-time engagement.
interests.description: This is a wide area, but my personal interests lies within cameras (especially webcams), video games, and game mechanics. I experiment with interactive design to tell new kinds of stories that may require more nuance or benefit from multiple states revealed at convenient moments.

about.bio: Maxime Perreault is an emerging digital multimedia artist from Quebec City and is now based in Tiohtiá:ke (Montreal). He holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts specialized in Computation Arts from Concordia University. Throughout his life, Maxime has been learning about 3D animation, programming, and creative technologies, allowing him to produce artwork ranging from illustrations, animations, and interactive installations. He is now working for Aboriginal Territories in Cyberspace as a workshop instructor and has started exhibiting his work in galleries. In parallel, from 2021 onwards, Maxime has been working as a tattoo artist under the alias of hd.maxi.
about.statement: Rooted in queer theory and influenced by my own personal experiences as a queer subject, my work speaks of identity, perception, and visibility. Through the combination of art, technology, and humanities, I want to push the boundaries of conventional artistic expression. Additionally, my love for tattooing allows me to help people define their identity through iconography. It is wildly validating to have people trust me with such permanent decisions and motivates me to be a better artist and person. Body modification serves as a huge inspiration for my digital media pieces, as it is closely tied to some of the recurrent themes I love to explore. My overall goal as an artist is to challenge our preconceived notions of normalcy. To achieve this, I combine a variety of techniques ranging from 3D animation and creative programming. I bring humanoid characters and otherworldly environments to life, I develop interactive installations, and I process images in experimental ways.
